newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK interbank rates steady to firmer in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: HK interbank rates steady to firmer in quiet trade.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady to firmer in quiet trading on Wednesday with activity focused on short-dated money as traders were watching the selection of the first leader of post-colonial Hong Kong, dealers said.
Overnight money was steady at 4-1/2 3/8 percent in a liquid market while three-month money rose slightly to 5-5/8 8/16 against 5-9/16 1/2 percent.
"Tung is elected but it doesn't have any impact in the interbank market," a dealer said.
Shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa scored a landslide victory in a vote earlier in the day.

Trading on government paper largely followed the weaker overnight close in U.S. Treasuries, dealers said. Short-date bill yields eased on steady demand while longer-dated note yields were slightly firmer.
One-week bill yields eased to 3.89 percent from 4.22 on Tuesday and one-month yielded 4.19 percent versus 4.37.
Three-year note yield was unchanged at 6.04 percent but the seven-year yield edged up two basis points to 6.98 percent and the longest 10-year note yielded 7.19 percent versus 7.17.
